items.title: Section: Equal Merit However Received, and What "Restraint" Itself Actually Means

items.zh: 若有如自所受而深護持，當知所生福德等無差別。又若起心往趣師所，慇懃勸請，方便發起禮敬等業，以正威儀在師前住，又以語言表宣所欲造作勝義，是名身表、語表業。意表業者，謂二前行。若自然受者，唯有意表業。若遠離思與不律儀相違，由遠離增上力故，與五根俱行，說名律儀。
items.en:
Second, revealing the merit involved. Whoever guards their precepts as deeply as if received from another should know the merit generated is no different at all.
Third, distinguishing the karma involved; first, receiving through another; first, bodily and verbal expression. Whoever, with a resolute mind, goes to the preceptor, earnestly requesting ordination, performing gestures of reverence and standing properly before the preceptor, and voices in words their resolve to undertake the precepts — this is called bodily and verbal expression.
Second, mental expression. Mental expression is what precedes both of these.
Second, spontaneous reception. Whoever receives the precepts spontaneously has only mental expression.
Fourth, defining the term. The intention to abstain, standing opposed to the unwholesome vow, joined with the five wholesome faculties sustained by the force of this abstaining intention, is called restraint.

items.title: Section: A Hundred Ways to Keep a Precept — By Degree, By Duration, and Now By Whether You Act, Urge, Praise, or Simply Rejoice

items.zh: 復次，當知由百行所攝而受律儀。謂於十種不善業道，少分離殺乃至少分遠離邪見，是名初十行。若多分離殺生乃至多分離邪見，是名第二十行。若全分離殺生乃至全分離邪見，是名第三十行。若少時離殺生，乃至離邪見，謂或一日一夜，或半月、一月，或至一年，是名第四十行。若多時離殺生乃至離邪見，謂過一年，不至命終，是名第五十行。若盡壽離殺生乃至離邪見，是名第六十行。若自離殺生乃至離邪見。是名第七十行。若於此事勸進他人，是名第八十行。若即於彼以無量門稱揚讚述，是名第九十行。若見離殺生者乃至離邪見者，深心慶悅、生大歡喜，是名第十十行。如是十十行，總說為百行，所生福量，當知亦爾。
items.en:
Fifth, clarifying its subsumption; first, presenting the hundred practices; first, stating it. Furthermore, one should know that the precepts received are subsumed under a hundred practices.
Second, distinguishing them; first, partial abstinence. With respect to the ten unwholesome courses of action, partially abstaining from killing up through wrong view constitutes the first ten practices.
Second, abstaining for the most part. Abstaining for the most part from killing up through wrong view constitutes the second ten. Third, complete abstinence. Abstaining completely from killing up through wrong view constitutes the third ten.
Fourth, brief abstinence. Abstaining briefly from killing up through wrong view — a single day and night, half a month, a month, or up to a year — constitutes the fourth ten.
Fifth, extended abstinence. Abstaining for an extended period from killing up through wrong view — beyond a year yet short of one's entire life — constitutes the fifth ten. Sixth, lifelong abstinence. Abstaining for one's entire remaining life from killing up through wrong view constitutes the sixth ten.
Seventh, abstaining oneself alone. Personally abstaining from killing up through wrong view constitutes the seventh ten. Eighth, urging others to abstain. Urging others towards this same matter constitutes the eighth ten.
Ninth, praising this abstinence. Praising and extolling this through countless approaches constitutes the ninth ten. Tenth, rejoicing in this abstinence. Seeing another abstain from killing up through wrong view, and giving rise to deep, heartfelt gladness and great joy, constitutes the tenth ten.
Second, concluding the measure of merit. These ten sets of ten, together called the hundred practices, generate a corresponding measure of merit that should be understood accordingly.

items.zh: 復次，律儀當知略有八種。

items.title: Section: Arousing, Receiving, and Guarding the Precepts — Two Forces That Keep a Vow Intact

items.zh: 一、能起律儀，二、攝受律儀，三、防護律儀，四、還引律儀，五、下品律儀，六、中品律儀，七、上品律儀，八、清淨律儀。若未正受，先作是心：我當定受如是遠離。是名能起律儀。若正攝受遠離戒時，名攝受律儀。從是已後，此遠離思五根攝受增上力故，恒與彼種子俱行，於時時間亦與現行俱行，即由五根所攝善思，如先所受律儀防護而轉。由此思故，或因親近惡友，或因煩惱增多，隨所生起惡現行欲，即便慚羞，速能捨離，勿彼令我違越所受，當墮惡趣。是名防護
items.en:
Second, explaining each; first, arousing restraint. Before actually receiving the precepts, first forming the thought, "I shall definitely receive this abstinence" — this is called arousing restraint.
Second, receiving restraint. Actually undertaking the precept of abstinence is called receiving restraint.
Third, guarding restraint; first, distinguishing its character; first, through wholesome intention. Thereafter, this abstaining intention, sustained by the force of the five wholesome faculties, continually infuses its own seed and, from time to time, manifests in actual conduct as well — it is this wholesome intention, subsumed under the five faculties, that guards the previously received precepts.
Second, through shame. Because of this intention, whenever, through contact with bad companions or mounting affliction, some unwholesome desire arises, one swiftly feels shame and quickly abandons it, so as not to violate what one has received and fall into a lower rebirth. Second, concluding the name. This is called guarding restraint.

items.title: Section: Three Kinds of Repentance — From Formal Confession to the Insight That Even the Guilty Mind Cannot Be Found

items.zh: 律儀。若時失念，諸惡現行，即便速疾令念安住，自懇自責，發露所犯，蠲除憂悔，後堅守護所受律儀，是名還引律儀。
items.en:
Fourth, restoring restraint. Whenever mindfulness lapses and unwholesome conduct manifests, swiftly re-establishing mindfulness, sincerely reproaching oneself, confessing the transgression openly, dispelling remorse, and afterwards firmly guarding the precepts received — this is called restoring restraint.
From the Universal Worthy Contemplation Sūtra: the entire ocean of karmic obstruction arises from deluded thought alone; whoever wishes to repent should sit upright and contemplate reality itself — every offence, like frost and dew, is dissolved by wisdom's own sun; therefore one should, with utmost sincerity, repent at the very root of the six senses.

items.title: Section: Inferior, Middling, and Superior Precept-Keeping — Measured by How Fully One Abstains, Encourages, and Rejoices

items.zh: 若於殺等諸惡業道，少分遠離，少時遠離，唯自遠離，不勸進他，不無量門稱揚讚述，亦不見彼諸同法者深心慶悅、多生歡喜，是名下品律儀。若於諸惡多分遠離，多時遠離，不至命終，自能遠離，亦勸進他，然於遠離不以無量門稱揚讚述，見同法者不深心慶悅、生大歡喜，是名中品律儀。若於諸惡一切分、一切時自能遠離，亦勸進他，以無量門稱揚讚述，見同法者深心慶悅、生大歡喜，是名上品律儀。
items.en:
Fifth, inferior restraint. Abstaining from killing and the rest only partially, only briefly, only personally, without urging others, without praising it through any means, and without deep gladness upon seeing a fellow practitioner's pure conduct — this is called inferior restraint.
Sixth, middling restraint. Abstaining for the most part, for an extended time short of one's whole life, personally abstaining and also urging others, yet without praising it through various means, and without deep gladness upon seeing a fellow practitioner's conduct — this is called middling restraint.
Seventh, superior restraint. Abstaining completely, for the whole of one's life, personally abstaining, urging others, praising it through countless approaches, and feeling deep gladness upon seeing a fellow practitioner's pure conduct — this is called superior restraint.

items.title: Section: Purified Restraint — How Meditative Concentration Itself Becomes a Kind of Precept, and Ten Levels of Keeping It

items.zh: 若即於此所受律儀能無缺犯以為依止，修無悔等乃至具足入初靜慮，由奢摩他能損伏力，損伏一切犯戒種子，是名靜慮律儀。如初靜慮，如是第二、第三、第四靜慮，當知亦爾。此中差別者，由遠分對治所攝奢摩他道轉深，損伏惡戒種子。
items.en:
Eighth, purified restraint; first, subsumed under meditative absorption; first, distinguishing its character; first, taking up the first meditative absorption. Relying on precepts already kept without breach, cultivating freedom from remorse and so on, up through fully entering the first meditative absorption, and thereby suppressing every seed of precept-violation through the power of calming meditation — this is called the restraint of meditative absorption.
Second, extending this to the other absorptions; first, showing the equivalence. As with the first meditative absorption, so too should the second, third, and fourth be understood. Second, revealing the difference. The difference here is that the suppression of bad-conduct seeds operates through the antidote of remote distancing as the path of calming meditation grows deeper.

items.title: Section: Four Kinds of Antidote — From Merely Weakening a Fault to Uprooting It Forever

items.zh: 當知此名初清淨力所引清淨律儀。
items.en: Second, concluding the name. One should know that this is called the purified restraint brought about by this first purifying power.

blocks.text: How vows are kept in degrees, how they are restored after a lapse, and how meditation itself becomes a kind of restraint.
Going to the preceptor, bowing, and voicing the resolve are bodily and verbal expression; mental expression precedes them. Master Cháng Bǎi: it is the mental activity before body and speech move.

Partially, mostly, completely; briefly, for long, lifelong; by oneself, by urging others, by praising, by rejoicing: each applies to the ten courses of action. Master Cháng Bǎi: abstaining from only the lighter grade of wrong conduct is "partial"; from all grades, "complete". (Untranslated, 0590a29: restraint is, in brief, of eight kinds.)

The first thought is "arousing" restraint; undertaking it is "receiving"; guarding it is "guarding"; recovering after a lapse is "restoring". Master Cháng Bǎi: the abstaining intention plants its own wholesome seed and also sets body and speech in motion.
Whenever mindfulness lapses, one swiftly restores it, reproaches oneself, confesses, dispels remorse, and guards the precepts firmly. Master Cháng Bǎi: 憂悔 is regret: disliking what one has done.
Master Cháng Bǎi: "at all times" means for the whole of one's life.

Absorption rests on precepts kept without breach and freedom from remorse. Master Cháng Bǎi: with remorse one cannot attain absorption; and on attaining it, one restrains oneself naturally. Yet worldly absorption only keeps the seeds of misconduct at a distance, "like a stone pressing on grass".
Notice how repentance is described: restore mindfulness quickly, confess, and *dispel* remorse. Lingering guilt is itself an obstacle to concentration.

quiz.q: What expressed karma is involved in reception through another and in spontaneous reception?
options: reception through another has only verbal expression; spontaneous reception has all three
reception through another has only bodily expression, spontaneous reception only verbal expression, and neither has mental expression at all
both alike are complete with bodily, verbal, and mental expression, with no difference
reception through another has bodily, verbal, and preceding mental expression; spontaneous reception has only mental expression
quiz.why: Going to the preceptor, bowing, and voicing one's resolve are bodily and verbal expression, and mental expression is what precedes both. Master Cháng Bǎi: mental expression is the mental activity before body and speech are set going. One who receives the precepts spontaneously has only mental expression, needing no bodily or verbal karma, unlike reception through another.

quiz.q: How are the "hundred practices" of the precepts counted?
options: a hundred of the most important among the monastic rules
across the ten courses of action, ten distinctions from partial abstinence to rejoicing give ten practices each: ten tens
the five, eight, and ten precepts added up and multiplied by the courses
keeping the precepts one day and night for a hundred days running
quiz.why: Each of ten ways of abstaining, namely partially, for the most part, completely, briefly, for an extended time, lifelong, by oneself, by urging others, by praising, and by rejoicing, applies to the ten courses of action, giving ten sets of ten. Master Cháng Bǎi adds that a hundred really expresses "many": beyond a hundred there could be a thousand or ten thousand.

quiz.q: On what basis does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish partial, most-part, and complete abstinence?
options: by length of time: a day is partial, a year is for the most part, and a whole lifetime is complete
by number of courses: three is partial, seven most-part, and ten complete
by people urged: one is partial, many most-part, and all complete
by grade of the ten evil deeds: abstaining from the lower is partial, lower and middle most-part, all three complete
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: abstaining from the lower grade of the ten unwholesome courses is partial abstinence; abstaining from lower and middle grades of evil conduct is abstinence for the most part; abstaining fully from all three grades is complete. Duration is a separate axis in the treatise, namely brief, extended, and lifelong abstinence.

quiz.q: Before actually receiving the precepts, one first thinks, "I shall definitely receive this abstinence." What is this called?
options: receiving restraint
arousing restraint
guarding restraint
restoring restraint
quiz.why: The treatise calls this first thought arousing restraint. Actually undertaking the precept is receiving restraint; guarding what was received is guarding restraint; and swiftly recovering after a lapse is restoring restraint. Master Cháng Bǎi on the third: guarding restraint means protecting it, keeping the precepts single-mindedly and without heedlessness.

quiz.q: The English has "continually infuses its own seed and, from time to time, manifests in actual conduct." How does this compare with the lecture?
options: the lecture says this intention has no seed, only manifestation, so the English "seed" is an addition to delete
彼種子 is the seed of bad conduct, which the intention accompanies, so "its own seed" reverses it
infuses is not literal for 與種子俱行 but fits the lecture's sense of infusing its own seed; joining manifestation means setting body and speech to guard against wrong
現行 is the expressed karma at the ceremony, occurring once, so "from time to time" is wrong
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the wholesome seed that it infuses as its own is what "accompanying its seed" means, and this abstaining intention setting in motion bodily and verbal karma that guards against wrong is "accompanying manifestation." The English "infuses" is an interpretation rather than the literal "accompanies," but it agrees with the Sub-commentary and the lecture, and is clearer than a word-for-word rendering.

quiz.q: Restoring restraint requires dispelling 憂悔. What does Master Cháng Bǎi say this is, and in what does it consist?
options: it is another name for the faculty of grief, left behind only in the first absorption, so one must enter it after a lapse
it is another name for regret: a practitioner, disliking what was done in the past, feels remorse
it is another name for torpor, in which the mind loses mindfulness
it is another name for faithlessness, which rejects cause and effect
quiz.why: Whenever mindfulness lapses, one swiftly re-establishes it, reproaches oneself, confesses, dispels remorse, and guards the precepts firmly. Master Cháng Bǎi: 憂悔 is another name for regret, meaning that a practitioner dislikes what was done in the past and so feels remorse. Note that the sūtra verse printed in this section of the English is the lecturer's citation, not the treatise.

quiz.q: The English has "for the whole of one's life" for 一切時 in superior restraint. Is this a fitting rendering?
options: unfitting: 一切時 means all three time-periods, so the English makes it too small
unfitting: 一切時 means the six watches of a day and night, not a lifetime, so the English makes it far too large
unfitting: 一切時 means both in and out of absorption, which the English omits
fitting: Master Cháng Bǎi says 一切時 means for life, so the English is clearer than a literal "at all times"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the "all times" meant here is for the whole of one's life; the keeper of the precepts abstains from the ten evil courses for life. Compared with a literal "at all times," the English "for the whole of one's life" brings out this sense and matches the "lifelong" of the hundred practices, a case where the translation helps the reader.

quiz.q: Regarding the restraint of meditative absorption, how does Master Cháng Bǎi relate precepts and concentration?
options: once absorption is attained precepts are no longer needed, so concentration ranks above them
precepts and concentration are independent; a precept-breaker can attain absorption just as well, and the precepts then simply recover
concentration precedes precepts, so one must attain absorption before qualifying to receive them
pure precepts free of remorse lead to absorption; absorption naturally leaves the ten evils, and precepts follow the concentrated mind
quiz.why: The treatise builds absorption on precepts kept without breach and freedom from remorse. Master Cháng Bǎi: with remorse one cannot attain absorption, so one whose precepts are impure cannot attain it. And on attaining absorption one naturally abstains from the ten evil courses; the mind being pure, the precepts are pure, and the precepts follow the concentrated mind.

quiz.q: The English has "operates through a more remote antidote." What is the problem?
options: 遠分對治 should be "nearby antidote," since absorption is what lies closest to afflictions, so the English is reversed and should be corrected
遠分對治 is the severing antidote, the seed being gone for good, so "remote" understates it
遠分對治 is the antidote of revulsion from hearing and reflection, so "antidote" should be "revulsion"
遠分對治 is the name of one of four antidotes, not a comparative; absorption only distances the seed, like a stone on grass, without severing it
quiz.why: The lecture lists four antidotes, and 遠分對治 is the name of the worldly one. Master Cháng Bǎi: on attaining absorption one can distance the seeds of bad conduct, only distancing without severing at the root, like a stone pressing on grass. The English "a more remote antidote" turns this name into a comparison, and the overview of the next section renders it differently.
